item.content:encoded:
Cine+Más SF Latino Film Festival & the San Francisco Public Library present MAXITA.

Experience the USA premiere of MAXITA, a compelling documentary from Brazil directed by Mariana Machado and Ana Maria Machado. Through Indigenous perspectives, environmental struggles, and spiritual connections to the land, the film explores the urgent fight to protect the planet and its natural resources.

Maxita: Film screening & Panel Discussion
Saturday, October 31, 2026 | 2-4p
Koret Auditorium, 100 Larkin St., SF
FREE – RSVP

Dirs. Mariana Machado, Ana Maria Machado, Brazil/Belgium, 2026, 70 mins runtime. C0-presented with the San Francisco Public Library

Visit CineMasSF.org for details on other films screening at the festival.

The 18th Cine+Más San Francisco Latino Film Festival brings films from across the U.S., Latin America and Spain to venues throughout San Francisco. This year’s lineup celebrates Latino stories and filmmakers through documentaries, dramas, comedies and films exploring culture, identity, family, migration and community.

ABOUT THE FILM

MAXITA
The shaman Davi Kopenawa Yanomami, one of the most important voices of Brazil’s Indigenous peoples, faces constant threats to his life as he embarks on a journey that takes him from the Amazon to the mining industry on the other side of the country, where he reunites with his old friend Ailton Krenak. Their encounter sheds light on the ongoing devastation of Brazil’s forests and natural resources, with consequences that extend far beyond the country’s borders. Traversing both the land and the spiritual plane, Davi’s journey invokes the maxita watimapë—the “earth eaters”—and offers a radical, urgent vision of humanity’s relationship with the planet.

About Cine+Más SF

The Cine+Más SF Latino Film Festival showcases the work of emerging and established filmmakers from the US, Latin America, Spain and Portugal. It is a celebration of the latest work coming out of the 20+ countries and the diaspora with which we share a bond.

item.content:encoded:
Free outdoor screening of Blue Beetle at SPARK Social SF, in partnership with Cine+Mas San Francisco Latino Film Festival!

Cine+Más: Blue Beetle Movie Night – A Celebration of Latino Cinema and Community!

Join us for a special outdoor movie night presented by SPARK Social SF and  Cine+Más San Francisco Latino Film Festival! We’re bringing Latino cinema, community, and a little movie magic under the stars at SPARK Social SF.

Grab your friends and family, enjoy some delicious food and drinks from the park, and settle in for a FREE screening of Blue Beetle on the SPARK Social SF Field.

Feature Film: Blue Beetle

Saturday, October 24 | 6:30 PM

SPARK Social SF | 601 Mission Bay Blvd North, San Francisco, CA 94158

Free Admission | Open to all!

Arrive early to grab a spot on the field, lay out your blanket, and get ready for an evening of movies, food, community, and fun under the San Francisco sky.

Food Trucks

Enjoy delicious bites from 15+ food trucks serving up a variety of meals and snacks throughout the evening. Grab dinner, drinks, and something to enjoy during the film!

About Cine+Más SF
Cine+Más San Francisco Latino Film Festival contributes to the Bay Area’s vibrant and diverse arts scene through its annual Latino Film Festival and year-round programming celebrating Latino arts and culture.
The festival showcases films by emerging and established filmmakers from the US, Latin America, Spain, and Portugal, highlighting creative works from around the world and across the Latino diaspora while fostering cultural exchange, connection, and community.

Don’t Miss Out!

RSVP for this FREE outdoor movie night and join SPARK Social SF and Cine+Más SF for an evening celebrating Latino cinema and community.
Bring your blanket, grab some food from the park, and get cozy for Blue Beetle under the stars!

item.content:encoded:
For its tenth anniversary, UNDISCOVERED SF is bringing the night market vibes back for the first time since the pandemic. In partnership with Victory Hall, formerly known as the iconic nightclub 330 Ritch, this year’s themes “Golden Hour” and “Made With Mahal,” make an intimate but electric return. With DJ sets by Hoochi, Vieux Carre, Boogie Brown, and performance by The Top Chefs of Live on The Stoop. Then step inside Victory Hall for a special exhibition honoring the history of 330 Ritch, the legendary nightclub that once made this block pulse after dark. The event is FREE for all ages and will take place Saturday, October 24, 2026, from 4-10 PM, on Ritch Street between Townsend and Brannan. The tenth anniversary edition returns the market’s roots to SoMa nightlife history, pairing that legacy with a new generation of vendors, chefs, and makers who have built their businesses through UNDSCVRD SF. This year’s curated vendors include food vendors-Mestiza, Little Skillet, Senor Sisig, Cafe 86, Ube Area, and more. Retailers include Malaya Botanicals, Mie Makes, Native Sol, Sunkissed Pinay and more.

Presented by Kultivate Labs

Tricks, Treats & Traditions in The Laurel
Saturday, October 24 (12pm-3pm)

 

The Laurel District Association invites families to Trick-or-Treat at MacArthur Boulevard businesses between 35th Avenue and High Street.

Meet up at Golondrinas Mexican Grill parking lot (4171 MacArthur Blvd) to get your free commemorative Trick-or-Treat bags (while supplies last) and to share in Día de los Muertos-themed crafts, community altar building, lawn games, face painting, DJ Tok@Ritmo, photo booth, and more!

 

Golondrinas Mexican Grill will be providing snacks and will be open for dining!

Free, all ages, and all are welcome. 

 

The adventure starts at Golondrinas Mexican Grill, 4171 MacArthur Blvd.

More info:  LaurelOakland.com
